nodes.content: Characterize bounds for dynamic treatment-regime effects under simultaneous unmeasured time-varying confounding and informative dropout.
requirements: Establish sharp identification bounds under explicit, separately interpretable confounding and dropout sensitivity constraints.
Construct confidence regions with at least 95% asymptotic coverage uniformly over the specified sensitivity class.

nodes.content: Optimize finite-history response-type linear programs under separate treatment Γ and dropout Λ ratio caps; project uniform 95% moment bands.
Can response-type linear programs yield sharp regime-effect bounds when Γ-constrained treatment selection and Λ-constrained dropout coexist?
For binary two-stage histories, every feasible Γ/Λ-constrained response-type extremum is realizable by a full-data law.
Enumerate binary two-stage response types, encode separate Γ/Λ ratio caps, construct extremal-law witnesses, and project uniformly valid 95% moment bands.
Enumerate binary two-stage response types; solve Γ=1.5, Λ=2 programs and check extremal full-data witnesses against observed margins.
At Γ=1.5, Λ=2, the LP's regime-effect upper bound was 0.74, but compatible full-data laws capped it at 0.68.
Cross-history consistency constraints reduce the Γ=1.5, Λ=2 upper bound from 0.74 to an attainable 0.68.
Add cross-history response-type coupling constraints, then globally optimize the Γ=1.5, Λ=2 upper bound and construct attaining laws.
With cross-history coupling, the certified upper bound was 0.68, matched by an admissible law within 10⁻⁶ at Γ=1.5, Λ=2.
Replace the uncoupled LP with cross-history coupling: its 0.74 endpoint is unattainable, while 0.68 has an admissible witness.
Project simultaneous 95% multinomial bands through the coupled program; simulate 2,000 datasets across Γ,Λ grids to assess worst-case coverage.
RegimeBounds v0.1 contains a coupled sharp-bound solver, projected 95% multinomial confidence regions, and Γ/Λ-grid coverage diagnostics.
Do projected multinomial bands maintain at least 95% coverage uniformly across Γ/Λ values and sparse treatment-dropout histories?
Profile full-data laws under separate treatment and dropout odds-ratio caps; invert least-favorable tests for uniform regime-effect inference.
Profile coupled full-data laws under separate Γ/Λ caps, certify sharp extrema, then calibrate least-favorable 95% tests uniformly.
Extend RegimeBounds v0.1 to profile coupled laws and benchmark least-favorable test inversion over 2,000 sparse-history simulations.
RegimeBounds v0.2 adds coupled-law profiling, least-favorable test inversion, and sparse-history coverage tables for Γ/Λ sensitivity grids.
Compare RegimeBounds v0.1 and v0.2 across 2,000 sparse-history replicates, recording minimum Γ/Λ-grid coverage and median region width.
Across 2,000 sparse-history replicates, minimum Γ/Λ-grid coverage was 95.8% for v0.2 versus 93.1% for v0.1.
Advance v0.2, pending uniform-coverage proof: coupled laws attain 0.68, and minimum simulated coverage reaches 95.8%.
Audit 95% uniform-coverage arguments for projected bands versus profiled tests over Γ∈[1,2], Λ∈[1,3], including sparse-cell boundaries.
Under 1/n rare-cell probabilities, asymptotically calibrated profiled tests cover 91%; exact multinomial-band projection covers ≥95% across Γ/Λ.
Can least-favorable test inversion handle 1/n rare-cell probabilities while preserving 95% uniform coverage and sharp coupled-law bounds?
Exact multinomial least-favorable test inversion over coupled laws preserves ≥95% coverage with 1/n cells without widening sharp identification bounds.
Implement exact least-favorable multinomial inversion after rare-cell failures; audit 1/n-cell coverage and preservation of coupled-law bounds.
Exact inversion attained 95.4% minimum simulated coverage with 1/n cells while preserving the coupled-law 0.68 identification endpoint.
Formulate shared-latent-history polynomial optimization with separate Γ/Λ odds caps and project exact multinomial bands onto regime effects.
Can sparse sum-of-squares relaxations certify globally sharp Γ/Λ bounds for three-stage regimes with shared latent histories?
Extend RegimeBounds v0.1 to three-stage histories; test degree-4 sparse SOS certificate gaps against feasible-law witnesses at Γ=1.5, Λ=2.
At Γ=1.5, Λ=2, degree-4 sparse SOS left a 0.02 certificate gap: upper bound 0.61 versus feasible 0.59.
The degree-4 gap reflects missing shared-history moment consistency; degree-6 sparse SOS with those constraints yields ≤0.001 certificate gaps.
Run degree-6 shared-history SOS and exact least-favorable inversion on three-stage Γ=1.5, Λ=2 simulations, recording certificate gaps and 1/n-cell coverage.
Degree-6 SOS narrowed the gap to 0.0008, but three-stage exact-inversion coverage was 93.6% with 1/n cells.
Restrict exact inversion to validated two-stage settings; use exact-band projection for three-stage inference pending calibration and SOS certification.
Certify SOS convergence and Γ/Λ-constrained extremal laws for three-stage bounds; project exact multinomial bands for uniform 95% coverage.
Run adaptive SOS until certificate gaps ≤10⁻⁴; project exact multinomial bands over three-stage Γ/Λ grids including 1/n cells.
RegimeBounds v0.3 records three-stage SOS certificates, flags gaps exceeding 10⁻⁴, and exports exact-band projected Γ/Λ confidence regions.
At Γ=1.5, Λ=2, three-stage shared-latent witnesses attained effect 0.59 and matched observed margins within 10⁻⁶.
Globally optimize history-consistent full-data laws by spatial branch-and-bound under separate Γ/Λ caps; project exact multinomial bands.
Outward-certified branch-and-bound projection of exact multinomial bands attains ≥95% uniform coverage for Γ∈[1,2], Λ∈[1,3], including 1/n cells.
Extend RegimeBounds v0.3 with outward-rounded branch-and-bound; verify exact-band containment and certify three-stage extrema across Γ/Λ grids, including 1/n cells.
Direct outward-certified projection covered only 94.1% of 2,000 three-stage 1/n-cell replicates; per-history exact bands lacked simultaneous calibration.
Replace v0.3's per-history bands with Bonferroni-calibrated exact bands; rerun certified projections over Γ/Λ grids with 1/n cells.
Across 2,000 three-stage 1/n-cell replicates, Bonferroni-calibrated projections reached 95.8% minimum Γ/Λ-grid coverage; simultaneous exact bands guarantee ≥95%.
Can outward-rounded branch-and-bound certify sharp three-stage regime-effect bounds where degree-6 SOS leaves a 0.0008 gap?
Outward-rounded branch-and-bound closes the Γ=1.5, Λ=2 three-stage certificate gap below 10⁻⁴ with admissible extremal-law witnesses.
After 94.1% undercoverage, use Bonferroni-calibrated bands and outward-rounded branch-and-bound to certify Γ=1.5, Λ=2 three-stage bounds within 10⁻⁴ of witnesses.
At Γ=1.5, Λ=2, outward-rounded branch-and-bound certified 0.59007 against an admissible 0.59000 witness, closing the gap to 7×10⁻⁵.
Adopt Bonferroni-calibrated branch-and-bound: uncalibrated coverage was 94.1%, calibrated coverage reached 95.8%, and the certification gap was 7×10⁻⁵.
Using calibrated simultaneous bands, prove outward-rounded branch-and-bound convergence to sharp three-stage extrema and certify Γ/Λ-grid witness gaps ≤10⁻⁴.
Initialize branch-and-bound from RegimeBounds v0.3 SOS certificates; test convergence and ≤10⁻⁴ witness gaps under Bonferroni-calibrated Γ/Λ projections.
RegimeBounds v0.4 contains outward-rounded Γ/Λ certificates, extremal-law witnesses, Bonferroni-calibrated 95% projections, and ≤10⁻⁴ gap flags.
Combine shared-latent trajectory optimization under separate Γ/Λ caps with 95% anytime-valid multinomial confidence sequences for adaptive monitoring.
Derive sharp coupled-law extrema with witnesses; prove 95% simultaneous multinomial sequences yield uniform Γ/Λ coverage under optional stopping.
Implement anytime multinomial sequences atop v0.4; benchmark stopped-time Γ/Λ coverage and width against v0.4 and v0.2 on 2,000 two-stage replicates.
Across 2,000 optionally stopped two-stage replicates, minimum Γ/Λ-grid coverage was 96.0% for anytime sequences versus 91.7% for v0.4.
Can trajectory-level Γ/Λ caps remain separately interpretable when treatment and dropout share latent causes across three stages?
Conditioning on shared latent histories keeps stagewise treatment-odds cap Γ and dropout-odds cap Λ separately adjustable without relaxing full-data consistency.
Using two-stage anytime coverage, vary three-stage shared-latent Γ/Λ caps independently; audit witness consistency, cap compliance, and stopped-time coverage.
Three-stage Γ-only and Λ-only perturbations each preserved shared-latent witnesses; cap violations were zero across 400 audited fits.
Provisionally extend calibrated branch-and-bound with anytime sequences: 96.0% two-stage stopped-time coverage; zero cap violations in 400 three-stage audits.
Prove branch-and-bound convergence to sharp shared-latent Γ/Λ bounds and uniform 95% anytime-sequence coverage under optional stopping.
Audit v0.4 certificates against v0.2 coupled-law profiles; prove convergence to sharp Γ/Λ bounds and uniform 95% anytime coverage.
RegimeBounds v0.5 documents sharp shared-latent Γ/Λ certificates, v0.2 cross-checks, and uniform 95% anytime confidence sequences.
